findings: Article 13(14) was incorrectly cited for free security updates; Annex I Part II (8) is the relevant provision.

Article 13(8) is generally at least five years or shorter expected use period; Article 13(9) is continued availability of each security update for ten years or remaining support period, whichever is longer.
Article 13(19) covers support-period end-date communication; Part II (8) contains a tailor-made product agreement exception.

findings: Annex I Part I (2)(d)/(e) quotation was accurate.
Universal disabling of all nonessential ports, protocol bans, and mandatory administrator opt-in were overclaims beyond the enacted wording.
Factory reset to original state is explicit; implementation must preserve safe configuration and be assessed for functional-safety impact.

findings: Raw Text Quote combined Article 13(8) support period and Annex I Part II (8) free security update delivery and was not verbatim.
Article 13(9) separately governs continued availability of each security update.
Annex I Part II (5) CVD policy is separate from free security update delivery in Part II (8).

findings: Annex I Part II (1) requires machine-readable SBOM with at least top-level dependencies.
No specific SPDX/CycloneDX format or universal transitive dependency inclusion is directly mandated by that point.
Part II (2) remediation without delay and Part II (4) fixed-vulnerability disclosure timing/exception are separate.

findings: SBOM source mapping is Annex I Part II (1), Annex VII 2(b)/8, Annex II point 9; Annex VI is simplified EU DoC.
SBOM is not mandatorily provided to every user; Annex II point 9 applies if manufacturer chooses to make it available.
All servo drives are not automatically Important Class I/II; classification requires Annex III product-function analysis.

findings: Annex I Part I (1)(e) is a nonexistent locator; access control is (2)(d), secure-by-default/reset is (2)(b).

findings: Final OJ DoS/availability locator is Annex I Part I (2)(h); point (2)(f) is integrity.

STO/SS1 behavior requires hazard analysis and functional-safety review; CRA DoS wording does not prescribe a stop function.
